raw.assessment: The incumbent plausibly checks physical compatibility during assembly and gives customers an initial arrangement, but those benefits are unmeasured. Its observed performance misses the time target; missing/incorrect-part reports and unpacking difficulties identify additional risks without establishing their causes. D2-O6 is a limiting observation: repeated three-compartment orders took seven to nine minutes, while mixed batches contained every extreme delay. This supports investigating selection and switching, but layout complexity remains a confound. Overlapping widths in D2-O5 also weaken a simple width-only explanation of insertion retries. The supplied evidence does not establish pilot success.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: a reusable order-specific parts tray, checked against the selected layout and color before insertion, reduces selection and reconciliation work in mixed batches.
openings.delta: Keep full assembly while replacing shared-bin selection during assembly with a visibly complete kit.
openings.prediction: Within the same layout and worker, total time including kitting falls through shorter selection/checking phases; insertion time changes little and component discrepancies decrease.
openings.probe: Use spare board for reusable trays. Counterbalance tray and current workflows within each layout and worker, including uncommon colors. Record selection, insertion, checking, packing, all preparation time, and audited component identity/count. Cost and schedule the bounded trial before use; stop if it threatens delivery.
assumptions: Tray preparation does not merely relocate equal or greater labor.
Implementation stays within 500 initial and 0.40 recurring cost caps; ordered geometry, contents, color and detachable joints remain intact.

openings.claim: The generic three-layout diagram may leave the short partition's location ambiguous even when every correct component is present.
openings.delta: Test an order-specific placement diagram on the existing instruction sheet.
openings.prediction: With verified complete kits, customers given the specific diagram make fewer short-partition placement errors; persistent mechanical insertion failures would weaken this account.
openings.probe: Allocate the ten participants between generic and specific diagrams, balancing ordered layouts. Record unaided completion, first short-partition placement, and insertion failures separately. Use the session diagnostically; its size cannot establish the 90% pilot target.
assumptions: The revised sheet replaces the existing sheet within the cost and deadline caps.
No component, footprint, capacity, accepted configuration or rearrangeability changes.

raw.assessment: Supplied observations suggest opportunities in part selection, layout interpretation and insertion, but do not establish their causes or separate their time costs. The capabilities below are hypotheses; neither has demonstrated pilot compliance.

openings.claim: A removable board carrier could preserve an order-specific spatial map from workshop kitting through customer assembly: every required partition occupies a labeled silhouette corresponding to its destination.
openings.delta: Combines component completeness checking with transfer of the selected arrangement. Dependencies are an accurate parts-to-layout map, distinguishable short-partition destinations, retention during packing, and a separate exterior-color check. Presently testable partial capability: a reusable bench template that exposes empty or incorrect part positions before assembly.
openings.prediction: Compared with current bins and diagrams, the template detects more deliberately omitted or substituted partitions; a customer carrier reduces short-partition placement requests without increasing total workshop time.
openings.probe: Use spare board for sample templates covering accepted layouts. Have both workers inspect balanced correct and seeded-error sample kits, timing selection, insertion, checking and packing separately. Randomize ten participants between carrier and existing-diagram conditions; record unaided ordered-layout completion. Cost the carrier before any pilot adoption.
assumptions: Carrier retention works without permanent bonds or changed partition geometry.
Initial spending stays within 500 and recurring additions within 0.40 per order.
Templates retain selected compartment counts and color; testing does not delay accepted deliveries.

openings.claim: A removable alignment guide could make first-attempt partition insertion reliable by controlling approach angle and supporting the base locally.
openings.delta: Speculative capability is temporary alignment during insertion. Dependencies are guide clearance, compatible slot locations and safe removal. A single spare-board guide tests the partial capability without redesigning supplied partitions.
openings.prediction: Guided insertion reduces retries after accounting for guide-placement time; equal performance would weaken the alignment explanation despite overlapping recorded widths.
openings.probe: Across up to 15 samples, randomize matched insertion locations to guided or ordinary insertion, balancing workers and partition types. Record retries, total insertion time, damage and subsequent dismantling. Avoid repeatedly testing worn slots.
assumptions: Approach alignment contributes to retries; width overlap alone does not establish this.
A reusable workshop guide fits the budget and delivery schedule while preserving product footprint, assortment, selected layout and color.

openings.claim: Reusable order trays reduce selection/reconciliation; retain assembly.
openings.probe: Counterbalance layout/worker/color; audit contents; time phases including preparation.
Compare diagrams with complete kits, balanced layouts; record unaided completion, placement and insertion failures.

openings.claim: Removable labeled carriers transfer the spatial map through packing to customers.
openings.discriminator: Bench error detection versus customer placement benefit.
openings.probe: Both workers inspect seeded omissions/substitutions; time phases, check color separately; randomize carrier/diagram users.

openings.claim: Removable guides control approach angle and support bases.
openings.probe: Randomize matched locations; balance workers/types; track time, retries, damage, dismantling; avoid worn slots.
openings.uncertainty: Width overlap cannot establish alignment causality.

post_distill.decision: Prioritize D1/D2. Share 15 samples/ten participants. Cost all probes: <=500 initial, <=0.40 recurring. Preserve 30x20 footprint, assortment, detachable partitions, accepted counts/colors and delivery; stop deadline-threatening trials. No pilot compliance established: 98% completeness, eight-minute median, 90% unaided completion remain unproven.
